c.tagline: Gateway to the emerald limestone karsts of UNESCO-listed Ha Long Bay

taxi.color: green and white (Mai Linh) or turquoise (Halong Taxi)
taxi.fareNote: Stick to reputable companies like Mai Linh; use the Grab app to avoid overcharging, which is common with unmetered street taxis near the bay.

emergency.note: Fire is 114. English-speaking assistance may be limited; for serious medical issues, transfer to Hanoi is common.

solo.f: Safety index is the main factor (70/100)

avoid.reason: Beware cut-rate cruise booking scams and bait-and-switch boat operators — book Ha Long Bay cruises through reputable agents.

hood_desc: The main tourist district on the western shore of Ha Long Bay, packed with hotels, seafood restaurants, and the Sun World Ha Long Complex cable car and amusement park. The lively Ha Long Night Market draws visitors for souvenirs and street food each evening. Most bay cruises depart from the nearby international cruise port.

The older, more local half of the city across the bay from Bai Chay, home to the municipal offices, the central market, and the port. It offers a grittier, more authentic slice of daily Vietnamese life away from the resort crowds.

A man-made peninsula turned resort island connected by a causeway, home to a large marina, a water park, and many of the wooden junk boats used for overnight bay cruises. It has a resort-town feel with hotels, restaurants, and evening entertainment.
A quieter district built around the revered Cua Ong Temple, a hillside pilgrimage site dedicated to a 13th-century general. It sees more domestic pilgrims than foreign tourists and has a slower pace.
A relaxed residential and beach area near Bai Chay, with a public beach, small seafood shacks, and fewer crowds than the main tourist strip. It's popular with locals for weekend swims.

water.note: Drink bottled or filtered water; tap water is not potable.

transit.map: no official transit app; Grab recommended
transit.note: Most visitors rely on hotel transfers, taxis, or Grab; walking along the Bai Chay and Hon Gai waterfronts is common.

train: No direct rail; nearest station is Hanoi, ~180km away
bus: Frequent buses and limousine vans from Hanoi (~2.5-3.5 hrs)
ferry: Boats and cruises depart from Tuan Chau Marina and Ha Long International Cruise Port for bay tours

airport.name: Van Don International Airport (VDO)
rentals: Limited local operators; hotel transfers common

tip.r: Tipping is not customary in Vietnam, but rounding up or 5-10% for good service in tourist restaurants is appreciated; tour guides and boat crews often expect a small tip.

food.name: Cha muc
food.desc: Ha Long's emblem dish: squid hand-pounded rather than blended, seasoned and fried into bouncy golden patties with a real chew.

places.name: Hong Hanh Restaurant
places.note: Widely named the best place in the city for authentic cha muc; also does mantis shrimp.

places.name: Ha Long Market
places.note: Buy it straight from the wok at the market stalls, still hot and crackling.

food.name: Banh cuon cha muc
food.desc: The local breakfast: silky steamed rice rolls with minced pork and wood-ear mushroom, served with squid cake and a light dipping sauce.

food.name: Bun be be
food.desc: Noodle soup built around be be, the mantis shrimp of Ha Long Bay, whose meat is sweeter and firmer than prawn.

food.name: Sam bien
food.desc: Horseshoe crab, a Quang Ninh delicacy, stir-fried with lemongrass and chilli, grilled, or fried into crisp cakes. For adventurous eaters.

places.name: Hong Hanh Restaurant

food.name: Ngan
food.desc: A Quang Ninh mangrove clam found almost nowhere else, grilled in the shell, steamed with lemongrass or dropped into a hotpot.

places.name: Ha Long Night Market
places.note: Evening seafood stalls grilling clams and oysters to order over charcoal.

food.name: Bay crab and grilled oysters
food.desc: Salt-roasted crab, steamed crab with ginger and cheese-topped grilled oysters, all pulled from the bay and its floating farms.

places.name: Cua Vang Restaurant

landmarks: Ha Long Bay
A UNESCO wonder of nearly two thousand jungle-topped limestone karsts rising from emerald water, best absorbed from the deck of an overnight cruise.
Sung Sot Cave (Surprise Cave)
The bay's grandest grotto, a cathedral-sized chamber of theatrically lit stalactites reached by a scenic stairway on Bo Hon Island.
Ti Top Island
A karst islet with a crescent beach and a 400-step summit lookout delivering the definitive panoramic photograph of Ha Long Bay.
Thien Cung Cave (Heavenly Palace Cave)
A fantastical cavern near the cruise port whose floodlit stalagmites conjure dragons and fairies from Vietnamese legend.
Bai Tho Mountain (Poem Mountain)
A limestone peak rising straight from the city, engraved with royal verses and famed for hard-earned rooftop views across the bay.
Sun World Ha Long and Queen Cable Car
A hilltop amusement complex reached by a record-breaking two-deck cable car, pairing a giant Ferris wheel with sweeping bay panoramas.
Cua Van Floating Village
One of the bay's last fishing communities, where rowing-boat tours glide among floating houses framed by towering karst walls.
Bai Chay Beach
Ha Long city's long promenade beach, a lively strip of sand, seafood restaurants and evening strolls beneath the Sun Wheel's lights.
Long Tien Pagoda
A colorful 1940s pagoda at the foot of Poem Mountain, its dragon-crowned gate marking Ha Long's most important Buddhist sanctuary.
Bai Tu Long Bay
Ha Long's quieter twin, an equally stunning maze of karsts and empty beaches favored by cruisers seeking the bay without the crowds.

train.note: Hạ Long sits at the end of a freight-dominated branch line from Kep and Yen Vien and has no useful scheduled passenger service, so in practice nobody arrives here by train. The nearest working railheads are Hai Phong and Hanoi, both on Vietnam Railways lines bookable at https://dsvn.vn/, and from either you finish the journey by road. Vietnam has no cross-border passenger trains in Quang Ninh province - the country's only international rail links run from Hanoi towards the Chinese frontier. Buses on the Hanoi-Hai Phong-Ha Long expressway are far faster than any rail option.

intl.to: Nanning (China) - daily 07:30 departure from the Nanning International Tourist Distribution Centre, about 8 hours via the Dongxing/Móng Cái border
intl.op: cross-border coach services — tickets bought at the Nanning terminal

bus.note: Most arrivals use Bãi Cháy bus station on the west side of the bay, or are dropped at hotels in Bãi Cháy and Hòn Gai by the limousine minibuses that dominate the Hanoi run; the expressway has cut Hanoi-Hạ Long to roughly 2.5 hours. FUTA Bus Lines (Phương Trang, https://futabus.vn/) and a crowd of smaller limousine operators sell seats online, while cheaper public coaches leave Hanoi's Mỹ Đình and Gia Lâm stations and can be paid for at the counter. Coming from China you can also cross at Móng Cái and take a local bus or taxi down the coast, about 4 hours.

intl.to: Cát Bà Island (Vietnam) - Tuần Châu Marina to Gia Luận, roughly 45-60 minutes
intl.op: Tuần Châu-Gia Luận car and passenger ferry — tickets at Tuần Châu Marina

intl.to: Quan Lạn, Minh Châu & Cô Tô islands (Vietnam) - high-speed boats from Cái Rồng pier at Vân Đồn, about 60 km east
intl.op: local high-speed boat operators — tickets at the pier

ferry.note: The practical boat link is the Tuần Châu-Gia Luận ferry to Cát Bà Island, which takes cars and motorbikes and runs several times a day from Tuần Châu Marina about 8 km west of Bãi Cháy; sailings thin out sharply in winter. Islands further east, such as Quan Lạn and Cô Tô, are reached from Cái Rồng pier at Vân Đồn rather than from Hạ Long itself. Everything else leaving Hạ Long's Tuần Châu and Hòn Gai harbours is a cruise or day-tour boat rather than scheduled transport, and there are no international sailings.

half.name: Yen Tu Mountain
half.blurb: A Buddhist pilgrimage mountain near Uong Bi with a cable car and forest temples, about an hour from Ha Long.

full.name: Cat Ba Island & Lan Ha Bay
full.blurb: The largest island in Ha Long Bay's own archipelago, reached by ferry, with limestone cliffs, beaches and a national park.

full.name: Tra Co Beach / Mong Cai
full.blurb: A long sandy beach at Vietnam's northeastern border town with China, about 1.5 hours from Ha Long via expressway.
